To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamics of Fc-DNA-C 6 chains is dominated by a slow free rotational diffusion of the DNA duplex around the C6 linker and that the dynamics of the F-capped dsDNA chains is fast enough to compete with DNA CT.
the dynamics of electron transport by free rotational motion of the ds-DNA chains is unexpectedly slow, and that electron transport by DNA CT is absent for the Fc-dssDNA-C6 systems studied here.

(i) the dynamics of Fc end-grafted dsDNA is much slower than expected from free rotation in solution; (ii) the dynamics of the Fcelectrode contact is modulated by accessibility of the Fc group to the electrode surface; and (iii) the dynamics of electron transport by DNA hinge motion is fast enough to, in principle, compete with electron transport by DNA CT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the motion of the ferrocenylated end of the 20-mer duplex DNA strand end-grafted to the surface via a C6 linker.
the study of charge transport in DNA by molecular dynamics of the redox-DNA strand.
the dynamics and electron transport of DNA chains end-grafting to gold electrode surfaces through a six-carbon linker.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dynamics of the Fec-dsDNA-C(6) system is dominated by a free rotational motion of the ds-DNA around its C6 linker, which is slow enough to be the rate-limiting step for electron transport in the Fc-dDNA-C(6)-electrode system.
the DNA duplexes in the Fc-dsdNA-C6 layers studied here are not able to conduct charge by a DNA CT mechanism, but that they are able to conduct charge via a free hinge motion mechanism.
the dynamics of Fc head motion is too slow to allow for DNA CT to occur, but is still fast enough to compete favorably with electron tunneling across the C6 linker.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

electron transport in dsDNA chains is possible by two mechanisms: (1) DNA CT, which is only present for very specific dsDNA systems, and (2) free hinge motion of dsDNA, which is present for any dsDNA chain, but is not necessarily fast enough to compete with DNA CT.
the dynamics of electron transport in DNA layers is dominated by the dynamics of the molecular layer and that the dynamics of the DNA duplex is not the only relevant factor in the dynamics of DNA CT.
the electron transport in the dsDNA-C6 systems is dominated by free hinge rotation of the dsDNA strand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of DNA duplexes anchored onto surfaces is a complex process, which is not easily predictable from simple considerations.
DNA duplexes end-grafted to a surface via a short linker behave as rigid rods and that the dynamics of their hinge motion is much slower than expected for freely rotating dsDNA in solution.

the dynamics of DNA duplexes end-grafted to surfaces via C6 linker is extremely slow, with a rotational diffusion coefficient that is at least three orders of magnitude smaller than expected for free rotational motion of dsDNA in aqueous solution.
